data.title: Show HN: Visual flow-based programming for Erlang, inspired by Node-RED
data.author: Towaway69
data.article_summary: Erlang-RED 是一个基于 Erlang 的可视化低代码编程环境，旨在替代 Node-RED 的 NodeJS 后端，实现与其流程代码的 100% 兼容（JavaScript 功能节点除外）。该项目利用 Erlang 的天然并发和消息传递优势，提升 Node-RED 的性能和并发处理能力。开发过程采用基于测试流的开发策略，通过一组测试流确保节点功能与 Node-RED 匹配。当前支持部分节点和功能，如 `catch`、`change`、`debug`、`delay`、`exec`、`function` 等，但一些复杂功能如动态延迟、多输出端口、JSONata 高级功能等尚未支持。项目架构体现了节点间的紧密联系，以确保正确的节点交互和异常处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Node-RED及其相关工具的优缺点、使用场景、技术实现和文档问题

不同观点：
• [nilslindemann] 认为Node-RED及其相关网站没有明确定义术语（如"flow"），建议提供术语表以便用户理解。
• [Arch-TK] 对Node-RED表示兴趣，但更倾向于使用Erlang而不是NodeJS，并询问是否存在专门解决事件驱动问题的DSL或库。
• [oersted] 认为Node-RED是一个用于并发处理的优秀工具，但指出NodeJS的单线程局限性，并建议使用如Rust等更专注于多线程的主流语言。
• [concerndc1tizen] 对类似项目及其使用的其他语言表示兴趣，并询问这种编程方式的主要问题，特别是大型程序是否难以处理。

补充讨论：
• [tzarko] 和 [aantix] 建议将示例部分或图片置于文档的更显眼位置，以帮助用户更好理解工具的视觉效果。
• [thinkyfish] 表示正在考虑使用FLENG而非Erlang来实现类似项目，并对Node-RED的启发表示赞赏。
• [bn-l] 请求推荐Erlang课程或书籍。
• [fnord77] 期望在一个视觉环境中看到更多图片以了解工具。
• [nisten] 以幽默方式表示社区想法一致。

技术问题与批评：
• [mystraline] 作为Node-RED的早期用户，指出尽管基础功能依旧良好，但其模块和库存在严重问题，尤其是版本管理不善导致的功能失效。

技术支持与建议：
• [paddy_m] 提出多项建议，包括解释什么是基于流的编程、明确项目的目标受众、定义操作符，以及建议制作JS实现和浏览器演示，并提出通过简单语言向非技术人员解释项目的挑战。

其他评论：
• [smartmic] 引用项目描述中的一句话，赞赏其不使用人工智能而依赖传统技术的方式，认为这是一种质量标志。

争议焦点：
• Node-RED使用的NodeJS单线程问题以及是否应采用如Erlang或Rust等其他语言实现多线程处理。
• Node-RED模块库的质量问题，尤其是版本管理和功能失效的批评。

总结：讨论围绕Node-RED工具的术语定义、技术实现、文档改进以及相关技术选型的优劣展开，用户对其视觉编程的潜力表示认可，但对其技术局限和库问题提出批评。

Erlang-RED - A Node-RED backend coded in Erlang
An experiment to replace Node-REDs existing NodeJS backend with an Erlang equivalent that is 100% compatible[1] to existing flow code.
The goal is bring the advantages of low-code visual flow-based programming to a programming language that is designed for message passing and concurrency from the ground up, hence Erlang.
[1] = 100% won't be possible since function nodes that are coded in Javascript aren't supported (or aren't intended to be supported - unless someone has a workaround)
Why?
Node-RED
is a amazing[*] tool for creating flows that describe concurrent processing, it is just a shame the NodeJS is single threaded. So why not use something that is multi-process from the ground up? Concurrency is guaranteed and included.
Also Erlang isn't the most understandable of programming language - unless one has fallen into in a
cauldron
of Prolog, spiced with Lisp.
So won't it be great to have the simplicity of low-code visual flow based programming and the performance (and concurrency) of Erlang?
[*] = amazing in the sense of
extendability
(Nodes can easily be added and developed by third parties),
understandability
(Node-RED
terminology
is straightforward) and
usability
(once a rectangle becomes a unit of computation and a line becomes a pathway for data flow)
Development Strategy
My development process is best described as
flow driven development
based around a set of
test flows
to ensure that node functionality is implemented correctly - meaning that it matches the existing Node-RED functionality.
Test flows are mirrored in a separate
repository
for better maintainability and also integration with existing Node-RED installations.
Architecture
The architecture, along with a background to Flow Based Programming and Node-RED has been
written
.
The codebase as it stands, has many interdependence because of testing flows:
assert nodes
need to know about
web-socket communication
, or because of the nature of nodes: the
complete
node needs to know of
completed messages
.
While the
exception node
needs to know about exceptions when they
happen
.
An architectural diagram of this interconnectedness would be probably be just as confusing as the code itself.
Supported Nodes & Features

Node

catches exception of selected nodes and of entire flows but not groups

msg.delay

executing and killing commands is supported  but only for commands in spawn mode and set on the node. Appending arguments to commands isn't supported. Timeouts are supported. Kill messages are also supported.

working for any Erlang. Stop and start also respected. Timeout and more than one output port isn't supported.

working

data.title: Rustls Server-Side Performance
data.author: jaas
data.article_summary: Rustls在服务器端的性能得到显著提升，特别是在多核处理器上能够几乎线性扩展，且不影响安全性。通过使用RwLock替代 mutex来处理票证加密密钥轮换，减少了并发连接握手时的争用。此外，将无状态恢复的默认票证数量从4个减少到2个，降低了带宽和CPU时间消耗。与OpenSSL相比，Rustls在处理大量并发连接时的平均和最差情况（P90、P99）延迟更低，整体性能更优。Rustls在保证内存安全的同时，提供了高效的TLS实现，适合广泛应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rustls与OpenSSL等其他SSL/TLS库的性能、安全性及其实际应用

不同观点：
• hardwaresofton认为Rust和Rustls在系统编程和SSL/TLS性能方面具有显著优势，尽管学习曲线陡峭，但其稳步的性能提升和内存安全性难以被其他语言或库复制。

• bastawhiz虽然不是Rust用户，但对Rustls项目表示赞赏，认为其在代码安全性和卫生方面优于BoringSSL等传统项目，并期待其在生产环境中的应用。
• dlgeek认为OpenSSL在性能敏感的应用中不再是理想选择，建议考虑Rustls或其他替代方案，如AWS的s2n-tls。
• pzmarzly引用了HAProxy的博客文章，认为OpenSSL的时代即将结束，但Rustls的C绑定尚未成熟，无法在生产中广泛使用。
• nyanpasu64讨论了在特定用例中使用Rust库（如crossbeam-epoch）的可能性，但担心其可能涉及不安全的代码编写和过早优化。
• thevivekshukla分享了其实际使用经验，指出在尝试将Rustls与Redis和Axum应用结合时遇到问题，最终转向原生TLS才成功。
• PoignardAzur对Rustls的名称感到困惑，误以为是关于已弃用的语言服务器。
• koakuma-chan简单表示Rustls速度非常快。
• lifeinthevoid对Rustls依赖于aws-lc和OpenSSL代码提出质疑，认为尽管OpenSSL的API混乱且容易引发错误，但其加密基元可能依然坚固。

• Rustls项目虽有前景，但在生产环境中的成熟度和适用性仍存在一定争议。

43972669.article_content:
Rustls Server-Side Performance
In past years, the
Rustls
project has been happy to receive substantial investments from the ISRG. One of our goals has been to improve performance without compromising on safety. We last posted about our
performance improvements
in October of 2024, and we're back to talk about another round of improvements.
What is Rustls?
Rustls is a memory safe TLS implementation with a focus on performance. It is production ready and used in a wide range of applications. You can read more about its history on
Wikipedia
.
It comes with a C API and
FIPS support
so that we can bring both memory safety and performance to a broad range of existing programs. This is important because OpenSSL and its derivatives, widely used across the Internet, have a long history of memory safety vulnerabilities with more being found this year. It's time for the Internet to move away from C-based TLS.
On the server
In our previous post we looked at handshake latency and traffic throughput for connections on the client and the server. While clients will usually have a small number of connections active at any time, TLS servers generally want to optimize for high utilization, supporting as many connections as possible at the same time. TLS server connections usually share a reference to a backing store, which can be used to resume sessions across connections for a substantial latency improvement in connection setup. Our goal is then to minimize the slowdown that sharing the resumption store imposes on individual connections.
We first validated the assumption that turning off resumption would allow linear scaling:
As our testing showed, Rustls manages to avoid any impact from scaling in this case, up to the 80 cores offered by the Ampere ARM hardware used in this test. This is similar to BoringSSL, which shows no impact -- although it spends more time per handshake. OpenSSL handshake latency deteriorates as it scales, although comparing OpenSSL versions shows that its development team have made strides to improve this, as well.
Resumption mechanisms
TLS supports two different resumption strategies:
Stateful resumption stores resumption state on the server in some kind of map (or database). The key into this map is sent across the wire. Because the key is relatively compact, this uses less bandwidth and therefore slightly reduces latency. On the other hand, it is harder to scale efficiently when multiple servers are serving the same potentially resuming clients.
Stateless resumption sends encrypted resumption state to the client. This is easy to horizontally scale because there is no server-side state, but the resumption state is a good deal larger, with an associated increase in bandwidth used (and the associated latency impact).
The resumption state that is sent to a client is commonly called a "ticket". Ticket encryption keys must be regularly rolled over because a key compromise destroys the security of all past and future tickets. In order to enable key rollover while supporting multiple concurrent sessions, Rustls 0.23.16 and earlier wrapped the encryption key in a mutex, which resulted in substantial contention as the number of concurrent server connection handshakes increased. In Rustls 0.23.17, we started using an RwLock instead, which limits contention to the short period when a key rollover happens (by default, every 6 hours).
Finally, we made another change in Rustls 0.23.17 to reduce the number of tickets sent by default when stateless resumption is enabled from 4 to 2, to align with the OpenSSL/BoringSSL default. This leads to doing less work both in terms of CPU time (encryption) and bandwidth used.
Handshake latency distribution
Apart from specific resumption concerns, we also compared Rustls to other TLS implementations in terms of the latency distribution experienced on the server: not just looking at the average latency, but also at worst-case (in this case, P90 and P99) latency. Rustls does quite well here:
While this chart shows full TLS 1.3 handshakes in particular, similar results were observed for other scenarios.
Conclusion
Current versions of Rustls show competitive performance when processing many connections at the same time on a server. Rustls servers scale almost linearly with the number of cores available, and server latency for the core TLS handshake handling is roughly 2x lower than OpenSSL in our benchmarks.

data.title: XTool – Cross-platform Xcode replacement
data.author: TheWiggles
data.article_summary: xtool 是一个跨平台工具（支持 Linux、Windows、macOS），旨在替代 Xcode，利用 Swift Package Manager (SwiftPM) 构建和部署 iOS 应用。它支持构建 SwiftPM 包为 iOS 应用、签名和安装应用、与 Apple Developer Services 进行交互等功能。用户可以通过命令行接口执行设置、开发、设备管理等操作，并能将 xtool 作为库集成到自己的应用中以与 Apple 服务和 iOS 设备交互。该项目基于 MIT 许可，拥有 1.7k 个星标和 42 个分支，主要由 Kabir Oberai 和 Nanashi 贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"Xcode替代工具"的评论和讨论

不同观点：
• **[lwouis]**：认为该工具声称的"Xcode替代"和"无Xcode开发"是误导性的。虽然工具本身不依赖Xcode的构建系统，但仍需要Xcode来获取iOS SDK和工具链。因此，这并不是真正的替代，而是一个旨在提供更好体验的额外层次。
• **[novoreorx]**：提到了类似的工具Sweetpad，并认为XTool在开发者体验（DX）上看起来更好，期望该项目能有更大发展。
• **[firecall]**：提到JetBrains的AppCode曾经是Xcode的智能替代方案，但AppCode在2022年12月14日之后不再作为商业产品提供。

补充讨论：
• **[zh3]**：提供了更多关于XTool的讨论链接，包括Swift论坛和Hacker News上的讨论。

data.title: Show HN: Merliot – plugging physical devices into LLMs
data.author: sfeldma
data.article_summary: Merliot Device Hub 是一个支持AI集成的设备管理中心，允许用户通过自然语言控制自制的物理设备，如安全摄像头、温度计等。该项目不支持普通智能设备，用户需使用树莓派、Arduino等组件自行制作设备。Hub采用分布式架构，确保数据隐私，且无需编写软件，提供可下载的设备固件。它作为网页应用程序运行，支持Docker部署，可在本地或云端运行。支持的设备平台包括树莓派、Arduino Nano rp2040 Connect等。项目提供了快速启动和安装指南，便于用户上手。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕将大型语言模型（LLMs）用于控制设备或机器人的讨论，包括技术可行性、应用场景、隐私问题及潜在风险。

不同观点：
• **技术潜力与应用幻想**：[rybosome] 表达了对使用LLMs和机器人结合的长期兴趣，尤其是用于舞台表演或音乐创作的潜力。他设想让LLMs控制机器人进行实时互动，并认为这将使表演更加生动有趣。但他也指出，实现这一设想需要大量时间和精力。
   
• **实际技术挑战**：[spaceport] 提到自己使用Nextcloud与Ollama集成的经验，指出尽管可以控制设备（如灯光和音乐），但要保证其持续稳定地工作是有难度的。此外，他反对将该系统与云端Claude连接，表达了对隐私的关注。

• **现有解决方案的比较**：[darkwater] 质疑该技术的创新性，认为Home Assistant已经在实现类似的功能，暗示该讨论可能没有提出新的技术突破。

• **隐私与架构复杂性**：[spaceport] 对文章中提到的隐私部分表示不满，认为其描述的中心化/去中心化架构过于复杂，建议简化为“本地托管，不连接云端”，以更直接的方式解决隐私问题。

• **其他潜在应用场景**：[chrisdalke] 提出将LLMs用于非正式对话控制机器人的“登月计划”式的设想，例如通过语音控制无人船移动。这一观点扩展了LLMs在不同领域应用的可能性。

补充讨论：
• **幽默与文化引用**：[neonwatty] 和 [imhoguy] 通过引用流行文化（如《Curb Your Enthusiasm》主题曲和电影《2001太空漫游》中的经典台词“Open the pod bay doors, HAL”），以幽默的方式参与讨论，暗示对技术发展潜在风险的担忧或调侃。

• **情绪反应**：[A4ET8a8uTh0_v2] 和 [fitsumbelay] 表达了对当前科技快速发展的感叹与认可，认为这是一个“奇怪但令人兴奋的时代”。[Kevcmk] 则以反问“What could go wrong?”来暗示潜在的技术风险或不可预见的问题。

争议焦点：
• 该技术的实际创新性与现有解决方案（如Home Assistant）的比较。
• 隐私问题，特别是云端连接与本地托管的选择及其复杂性。

MERLIOT DEVICE HUB
Merliot
Hub is an
AI-integrated device hub.
What does that mean?  It means you can control and interact with your physical
devices, your security cameras, your thermometer, seamlessly using natural
language from an LLM host such as
Claude Desktop
or
Cursor
.  The hub is a gateway between AI and the
physical world.
What could go wrong?
Devices
Which devices?  Sorry, not any of the consumer-grade Smart devices such as
Smart security cameras, Smart lights, and Smart thermostats.  Merliot Hub only
supports devices you build.  You build devices from hobby-grade components
which are readily available, like Raspberry Pis, Arduinos, buttons, relays, and
sensors.  You need maker-level skills to build the devices.  The hub includes a
parts list and instructions for building each device.  There is no software to
write; the hub includes the downloadable device firmware.
FEATURES
Privacy
Merliot Hub uses a distributed architecture rather than a centralized
architecture, eliminating third-party access to your devices' data. You
install and maintain your own hub and devices.  No one else has access.  Your
data is private.  Your data can't be sold, shared, stored, analyzed, or
surveilled by third parties.
Read more
.
Web App
Merliot hub is a web app.  There is no phone app.  You can use any
web browser on any device, including your phone, to access your hub,
locally or over the internet.  Try the
demo
to get a feel for the UI.
AI-Integration
Merliot Hub is a Model Context Protocol (
MCP
)
server.  The MCP server lets you plug your Merliot Hub into LLM hosts such as
Claude or Cursor.  From there, you can chat with the hub using natural language:
"List all of the devices in a tree view"
"Add a new gps device"
"Turn on all the relays"
"Show the instructions on how to deploy a qrcode device"
Cloud-Ready
Merliot Hub is packaged as a Docker image so you can run your hub
anywhere you can run a Docker image, locally on your own laptop or server
using Docker Desktop, or on the cloud.  See
install
guide for more info.  The docker
image requires a minimal VM: 0.1vCPU, 256MB RAM, 256MB disk.  Koyeb offers a
FREE
VM suitable for running a hub in the cloud.
SUPPORTED DEVICES TARGETS
Merliot Hub devices are built from one or more target platforms:
Raspberry Pi (models 3, 4, 5, and Zero 2W)
Arduino Nano rp2040 Connect
Adafruit PyPortal
Koyeb (cloud)
Linux x86-64
QUICK START
See the official
Quick Start
and
Install
guides for more info.
Install with Docker
$ sudo docker run -p 8000:8000 merliot/hub
Browse to
http://localhost:8000
to view hub.
Install on Cloud
Run a FREE hub instance on
Koyeb
.  Use this one-click button to get started:
Run from Source
$ git clone https://github.com/merliot/hub.git
$ cd hub
$ go run ./cmd
Browse to
http://localhost:8000
to view hub.
CONTRIBUTING
PRs/Issues welcomed.
I'd like to see others build cool devices to share and to add to the project.
TESTING
$ go test ./test/...
LICENSE
BSD 3-Clause License
CONTACT
Email:
contact@merliot.io
X:
@merliotio
Slack:
#merliot
CREDITS
Merliot is written in
Go
,
TinyGo
, and
htmx.
Thank you to those who built and maintain these fine tools.

data.title: New high-quality hash measures 71GB/s on M4
data.author: nicoshev11
data.article_summary: Rapidhash 是一个非常快速、高质量且跨平台的哈希算法，是 wyhash 的官方 successor。它在多种系统（AMD64 和 AArch64）及编译器（gcc、clang、icx、MSVC）上表现优异，不依赖特定机器指令集。Rapidhash 在 SMHasher 和 SMHasher3 测试中表现卓越，速度超越 70GB/s，并在碰撞测试中表现出接近理想的碰撞概率。与 xxh3 相比，rapidhash 在多项性能测试中均表现出色，尤其是在小尺寸键值的哈希计算中。Rapidhash 的平均延迟和峰值吞吐量在多个硬件平台上均领先于 xxh3。所有测试和实验代码可在项目的 collisions 和 bench 文件夹中找到。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同技术背景下对"rapidhash"功能的评价与应用讨论

不同观点：
• **支持rapidhash作为小键的高效哈希函数**：jandrewrogers认为rapidhash在小键哈希功能上是目前最先进的，没有发现更好的替代方案。对于批量哈希，虽然有其他函数，但它们在速度和强度上都不如rapidhash。

• **对速度提升的价值持保留态度**：aidenn0指出，对于很多场景，现有的哈希函数（如xxhash）已经足够快，尤其是对大键而言。为了节省几十皮秒的性能提升而更换哈希函数并不值得。

• **提出更快、更强的替代方案**：rurban提到rapidhash在smhasher基准测试中已经不是最快的，umash和gxhash在速度上更具优势，特别是gxhash比rapidhash快两倍。不过，rapidhash由于体积小，对哈希表更友好。

• **对可变长度字符串的性能比较**：curiouscoding分享了他们的经验，指出gxhash在处理10到30个字符长度的随机字符串时比xxhash更快，推测这是因为gxhash能一次处理多达32个字符，避免了分支预测失败。

补充讨论：
• **实际应用场景的疑问**：mertleee直接质疑rapidhash的实际应用场景，表明对该技术实际用途的困惑。

• **对性能数据的选择性展示提出质疑**：eqvinox质疑为什么"性能"部分的数字几乎全是针对AArch64架构，而没有AMD64的性能数据。

• **对缓存友好性的关注**：wpollock关注rapidhash是否对缓存友好，暗示对内存性能影响的关心。

• **对讨论方向的失望**：bandrami表示对讨论的前四句话有期待，但后续讨论方向令其失望，暗示对技术深度讨论的期待未被满足。

争议焦点：
• **哈希函数的速度与实际需求之间的权衡**：一方认为rapidhash提供了最佳的小键哈希方案，而另一方则认为在现有速度已经足够的情况下，微小的性能提升并不值得更换技术。

Collision-based hash quality study
A perfect hash function distributes its domain uniformly onto the image.
When the domain's cardinality is a multiple of the image's cardinality, each potential output has the same probability of being produced.
A function producing 64-bit hashes should have a
$p=1/2^{64}$
of generating each output.
If we compute
$n$
hashes, the expected amount of collisions should be the number of unique input pairs times the probability of producing a given hash.
This should be
$(n*(n-1))/2 * 1/2^{64}$
, or simplified:
$(n*(n-1))/2^{65}$
.
In the case of hashing
$15*2^{30}$
(~16.1B) different keys, we should expect to see
$7.03$
collisions.
We present an experiment in which we use rapidhash to hash
$77$
datasets of
$15*2^{30}$
(15Gi) keys each.
For each dataset, the amount of collisions produced is recorded as measurement.
Ideally, the average among measurements should be
$7.031$
and the results collection should be a binomial distribution.
We obtained a mean value of
$8.026$
, just
$14$
% over
$7.031$
.
Each dataset individual result and the collisions test program can be found in the
collisions folder
.
The default seed
$0$
was used in all experiments.

43981971.article_summary: Rapidhash 是一个非常快速、高质量且跨平台的哈希算法，是 wyhash 的官方 successor。它在多种系统（AMD64 和 AArch64）及编译器（gcc、clang、icx、MSVC）上表现优异，不依赖特定机器指令集。Rapidhash 在 SMHasher 和 SMHasher3 测试中表现卓越，速度超越 70GB/s，并在碰撞测试中表现出接近理想的碰撞概率。与 xxh3 相比，rapidhash 在多项性能测试中均表现出色，尤其是在小尺寸键值的哈希计算中。Rapidhash 的平均延迟和峰值吞吐量在多个硬件平台上均领先于 xxh3。所有测试和实验代码可在项目的 collisions 和 bench 文件夹中找到。

data.title: Google worried it couldn't control how Israel uses Project Nimbus, files reveal
data.author: zhengiszen
data.article_summary: 谷歌在与以色列签署利润丰厚且具争议的Project Nimbus协议前，已知晓其无法控制以色列及其军方如何使用其强大的云计算技术。根据《The Intercept》获得的内部报告，谷歌明白向一个长期被指控侵犯人权的国家提供先进技术存在风险。报告指出，谷歌无法完全监控或阻止以色列利用其软件伤害巴勒斯坦人，且该协议可能要求谷歌在其他国家对以色列的技术使用进行刑事调查时设置障碍。此外，协议还要求与以色列安全部门密切合作，这在谷歌与其他国家的协议中是前所未有的。第三方顾问建议谷歌不要向以色列提供机器学习和人工智能工具。国际法律专家认为，谷歌对风险的认知及其未能进行标准尽职调查可能导致法律责任。谷歌拒绝回应有关其对以色列使用其服务可见度或对Project Nimbus控制权的问题。

44010922.article_content:
Photo illustration: Fei Liu / Photo: Zain JAAFAR/AFP
Before signing its
lucrative and controversial Project Nimbus deal with Israel, Google knew it couldn’t control what the nation and its military would do with the powerful cloud-computing technology, a confidential internal report obtained by The Intercept reveals.
The report makes explicit the extent to which the tech giant understood the risk of providing state-of-the-art cloud and machine learning tools to a nation long accused of systemic human rights violations and wartime atrocities. Not only would Google be unable to fully monitor or prevent Israel from using its software to harm Palestinians, but the report also notes that the contract could obligate Google to stonewall criminal investigations by other nations into Israel’s use of its technology. And it would require close collaboration with the Israeli security establishment — including joint drills and intelligence sharing — that was unprecedented in Google’s deals with other nations.
A third-party consultant Google hired to vet the deal recommended that the company withhold machine learning and artificial intelligence tools from Israel because of these risk factors.
Three international law experts who spoke with The Intercept said that Google’s awareness of the risks and foreknowledge that it could not conduct standard due diligence may pose legal liability for the company. The rarely discussed question of legal culpability has grown in significance as Israel enters the third year of what has widely been acknowledged as a
genocide in Gaza
— with shareholders pressing the company to conduct due diligence on whether its technology contributes to human rights abuses.
“They’re aware of the risk that their products might be used for rights violations,” said León Castellanos-Jankiewicz, a lawyer with the Asser Institute for International and European Law in The Hague, who reviewed portions of the report. “At the same time, they will have limited ability to identify and ultimately mitigate these risks.”
Google declined to answer any of a list of detailed questions sent by The Intercept about the company’s visibility into Israel’s use of its services or what control it has over Project Nimbus.
Company spokesperson Denise Duffy-Parkes instead responded with a verbatim copy of a statement that Google provided for a different article last year. “We’ve been very clear about the Nimbus contract, what it’s directed to, and the Terms of Service and Acceptable Use Policy that govern it. Nothing has changed.”
Portions of the internal document were
first reported
by the New York Times, but Google’s acknowledged inability to oversee Israel’s usage of its tools has not previously been disclosed.
Most Read
ICE Duped a Federal Judge Into Allowing Raid on Columbia Student Dorms
Shawn Musgrave
Trump Is Building a Global Gulag for Immigrants Captured by ICE
Nick Turse, Jonah Valdez
Republicans Sneak Nonprofit Killer Bill Into the Tail End of Trump’s 389-Page Tax Plan
Noah Hurowitz
In January 2021
, just three months before Google won the Nimbus contract alongside Amazon, the company’s cloud computing executives faced a dilemma.
The Project Nimbus contract — then code-named “Selenite” at Google — was a clear moneymaker. According to the report, which provides an assessment of the risks and rewards of this venture, Google estimated a bespoke cloud data center for Israel, subject to Israeli sovereignty and law, could reap $3.3 billion between 2023 and 2027, not only by selling to Israel’s military but also its financial sector and corporations like pharmaceutical giant Teva.
But given decades of transgressions against international law by Israeli military and intelligence forces it was now supplying, the company acknowledged that the deal was not without peril. “Google Cloud Services could be used for, or linked to, the facilitation of human rights violations, including Israeli activity in the West Bank,” resulting in “reputation harm,” the company warned.
In the report, Google acknowledged the urgency of mitigating these risks, both to the human rights of Palestinians and Google’s public image, through due diligence and enforcement of the company’s terms of service, which forbid certain acts of destruction and criminality.
But the report makes clear a profound obstacle to any attempt at oversight: The Project Nimbus contract is written in such a way that Google would be largely kept in the dark about what exactly its customer was up to, and should any abuses ever come to light, obstructed from doing anything about them.
Read our complete coverage
Israel’s War on Gaza
The document lays out the limitations in stark terms.
Google would only be given “very limited visibility” into how its software would be used. The company was “not permitted to restrict the types of services and information that the Government (including the Ministry of Defense and Israeli Security Agency) chooses to migrate” to the cloud.

data.title: Catalog of Novel Operating Systems
data.author: prathyvsh
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由prathyvsh创建的名为"os-catalog"的项目，该项目旨在收录一些新颖的操作系统。文章提到，在笔记应用热潮之后，许多人开始大胆开发新的操作系统，并列举了过去一些具有独特交互语言的操作系统，如AmigaOS、NeXTSTEP等。文中详细介绍了几个新颖的操作系统项目，包括UXN、Playbit、Folk.computer、Nette.io、Interim、Mezzano、ChrysalLisp、RayvnOS、RedoxOS、DesktopNeo、MercuryOS、Bedrock.computer等。每个项目都有其独特的特性和创新，例如UXN的个人计算栈、Playbit的全新计算机栈尝试、以及MercuryOS基于意图的重新思考。文章还提供了相关文档和项目的链接，供读者进一步探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：操作系统的不同形式与功能，包括操作系统（OS）与操作环境（OE）的区别、专门化系统、用户界面（UI）的创新以及低层技术挑战等。

不同观点：
• **操作环境（OE） vs 操作系统（OS）**：
   - **gnramires** 认为，开发全新的操作系统并非总是必要，建议开发"操作环境"（OE），它可以作为应用程序在现有主机操作系统上运行，从而复用主机系统的功能并提供新的用户界面。例子包括Emacs、浏览器以及像pico-8和mini micro等"虚拟电脑"。
   - 该观点强调了开发低层系统（如文件系统、设备驱动等）的复杂性，以及现有系统如Linux的广泛设备支持。

• **对专门化系统的兴趣**：
   - **MomsAVoxell** 提到对老式专门系统（如Wang Imaging System）的兴趣，认为这些系统在特定领域（如档案数字化）非常实用，并表达了对复古计算的热情。
   - **diego_moita** 强调了操作系统不仅限于桌面和移动设备，还应关注更专门的设备，如电子阅读器、路由器、智能手表等，并指出这些设备上发生的有趣开发工作。

• **特定技术需求的操作系统**：
   - **alphazard** 指出了seL4和Helios等具有强安全性和沙盒功能的操作系统的重要性，批评了Linux等单体内核系统在文件系统和网络方面的停滞，以及开发过程中的组织政治问题。
   - **Lerc** 关注多处理器系统的支持，询问是否存在为数百或数千处理器设计的操作系统。

• **用户界面创新的需求**：
   - **serhack_** 希望看到更多非WIMP（窗口、图标、菜单、指点设备）基础的用户界面示例。
   - **justanothersys** 提到自己创建的网页项目（aesthetic.computer），展示了对操作系统UI创新的持续探索。

补充讨论：
• **对现有列表的补充与批评**：
   - **maxlin** 建议将SerenityOS纳入讨论，认为它是完全从零开发的、且代码可完全理解的操作系统。
   - **jeffbee** 批评该列表更像是"UI演示"，而非真正的操作系统，并表达了对实际项目的期望。
   - **rubitxxx3** 认为列表不够全面，期待更多CS学生和爱好者的项目。

• **其他提及**：
   - **zhainya** 提到了TempleOS，作为另一个值得注意的操作系统例子。
   - **gitroom** 表达了对老式和怪异操作系统探索的喜爱，激发了对个人旧项目的兴趣。

争议焦点：操作系统的定义与范围，尤其是操作环境与传统操作系统的区别，以及哪些系统应被纳入讨论。此外，操作系统UI的创新与底层技术改进之间的优先级也是讨论的重点。

Novel Operating Systems Catalog
Catalogue of novel operating systems
Somewhere after the fall in popularity of note-taking apps, perhaps recognizing that just note-taking is not enough and the deafening hype of LLMs, there was a sweet period of lull when a lot of people started boldly building new operating systems. This is a catalogue of such operating systems that I have come across. In the past, before the commercialization of computers, we had a plethora of operating systems with unique languages to interact with computers, like AmigaOS, Symbolics, SunOS, MULTICS, Burroughs, Meneut, BeOS PARC, Star, Oberon, Plan9, NeXTSTEP, OS/2, PL/8, Inferno, QNX, RISCOS etc. This spirit can only be glimpsed in pockets, and kudos to all those who keep the fire alive!
UXN
Perhaps the best one to start off this catalog is the UXN/Varvara personal computing stack of
100 Rabbits
. Such a great couple with such a radical vision!
They have documented their rationale in these two documents:
Tools Ecosystem
Weathering Software Winter
Documents related to UXN can be obtained here:
https://github.com/hundredrabbits/awesome-uxn?tab=readme-ov-file
Playbit
Daring effort from
Rasmus Andersson
and team to reinvent the computer stack.
And alpha version available
here
.
Folk.computer
Omar Rizwan and Andreas Cuérvo
Nette.io
Nette.io by
Pawel Ceranka
positions itself as a research OS for the web.
Interim
Something about Lisp draws people into construct OSes from ground up. Perhaps it is the simplicity of the language that acts as the foundation. Here‘s Interim, one of our favourite minimal OSes constructed with Lisp.
Mezzano
An OS written in CommonLisp
ChrysalLisp
ChrysaLisp is amulti-threaded, multi-core, multi-user parallel OS with features such as a GUI, terminal, OO Assembler, class libraries, C-Script compiler, Lisp interpreter, debugger, profiler, vector font engine, and more.

44012615.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由prathyvsh创建的名为"os-catalog"的项目，该项目旨在收录一些新颖的操作系统。文章提到，在笔记应用热潮之后，许多人开始大胆开发新的操作系统，并列举了过去一些具有独特交互语言的操作系统，如AmigaOS、NeXTSTEP等。文中详细介绍了几个新颖的操作系统项目，包括UXN、Playbit、Folk.computer、Nette.io、Interim、Mezzano、ChrysalLisp、RayvnOS、RedoxOS、DesktopNeo、MercuryOS、Bedrock.computer等。每个项目都有其独特的特性和创新，例如UXN的个人计算栈、Playbit的全新计算机栈尝试、以及MercuryOS基于意图的重新思考。文章还提供了相关文档和项目的链接，供读者进一步探索。

主要讨论点：操作系统的不同形式与功能，包括操作系统（OS）与操作环境（OE）的区别、专门化系统、用户界面（UI）的创新以及低层技术挑战等。

不同观点：
• **操作环境（OE） vs 操作系统（OS）**：
   - **gnramires** 认为，开发全新的操作系统并非总是必要，建议开发"操作环境"（OE），它可以作为应用程序在现有主机操作系统上运行，从而复用主机系统的功能并提供新的用户界面。例子包括Emacs、浏览器以及像pico-8和mini micro等"虚拟电脑"。
   - 该观点强调了开发低层系统（如文件系统、设备驱动等）的复杂性，以及现有系统如Linux的广泛设备支持。

• **对专门化系统的兴趣**：
   - **MomsAVoxell** 提到对老式专门系统（如Wang Imaging System）的兴趣，认为这些系统在特定领域（如档案数字化）非常实用，并表达了对复古计算的热情。
   - **diego_moita** 强调了操作系统不仅限于桌面和移动设备，还应关注更专门的设备，如电子阅读器、路由器、智能手表等，并指出这些设备上发生的有趣开发工作。

• **特定技术需求的操作系统**：
   - **alphazard** 指出了seL4和Helios等具有强安全性和沙盒功能的操作系统的重要性，批评了Linux等单体内核系统在文件系统和网络方面的停滞，以及开发过程中的组织政治问题。
   - **Lerc** 关注多处理器系统的支持，询问是否存在为数百或数千处理器设计的操作系统。

• **用户界面创新的需求**：
   - **serhack_** 希望看到更多非WIMP（窗口、图标、菜单、指点设备）基础的用户界面示例。
   - **justanothersys** 提到自己创建的网页项目（aesthetic.computer），展示了对操作系统UI创新的持续探索。

补充讨论：
• **对现有列表的补充与批评**：
   - **maxlin** 建议将SerenityOS纳入讨论，认为它是完全从零开发的、且代码可完全理解的操作系统。
   - **jeffbee** 批评该列表更像是"UI演示"，而非真正的操作系统，并表达了对实际项目的期望。
   - **rubitxxx3** 认为列表不够全面，期待更多CS学生和爱好者的项目。

• **其他提及**：
   - **zhainya** 提到了TempleOS，作为另一个值得注意的操作系统例子。
   - **gitroom** 表达了对老式和怪异操作系统探索的喜爱，激发了对个人旧项目的兴趣。

争议焦点：操作系统的定义与范围，尤其是操作环境与传统操作系统的区别，以及哪些系统应被纳入讨论。此外，操作系统UI的创新与底层技术改进之间的优先级也是讨论的重点。

data.title: MinorMiner: We turn your kid's maths homework into Bitcoin
data.author: pimterry
data.article_summary: MinorMiner是一个让学龄儿童通过数学作业来挖比特币的平台。创始人Hobert Reaton认为，学生在完成大量计算作业时浪费了计算能力，因此他创建了MinorMiner，将学生的计算成果用于比特币挖矿。比特币挖矿目前依赖于解决复杂的数学谜题，而MinorMiner将这些问题简化为基本的算术题，学生在不知情的情况下通过完成这些题目帮助挖矿。平台通过在线数学测验将题目分发给学生，平台处理其余部分，从而将学生的努力转化为“数字黄金”。这一创新不仅让孩子们的作业变得有价值，还减少了传统比特币挖矿的高能耗问题。

MinorMiner: we turn your kid's maths homework into Bitcoin
14 May 2025
Hello! Hello! Welcome, welcome. My name is Hobert Reaton, and I’m here in this shabby motel conference room to present you with yet
another
once-in-a-lifetime
investment opportunity.
Look at this picture. Tell me what you see:
Do you see learning? Self-improvement? The future leaders of our country?
I’ll tell you what I see: wasted computing power.
Between the ages of 5 and 18, the average child in full-time education completes about 5 maths worksheets a week. Each worksheet has 20 questions. This means that over the course of their school career, every single one of our kids performs about 80,000 calculations.
At the moment we completely waste their work. A student figures out that 5+5=10 and 7x7=49. This motivates them; they’re energised by their success. But then what do we do with the fruits of their labour? Nothing! We throw the fruit away, to rot in the void. “We knew that already,” we tell our children. “Your ideas don’t matter.” Unlike the rest of society, I believe that kids deserve to feel appreciated. I believe that their achievements are valuable.
That’s why I founded MinorMiner.
What is MinorMiner?
MinorMiner is a platform that allows school-age children to monetise their maths homework by using it to mine Bitcoin. Yes, you heard me. We send children their homework, they crunch through it, and then together we transform their sweat into digital gold. This isn’t some rinky-dink incentive program where we bribe children to care about multiplication. Homework is the essential raw material that feeds our machine. We need these kids. No kids; no Bitcoin.
In order to understand the innovation that makes MinorMiner possible, we first need to understand how Bitcoin is mined today. Right now, people mine Bitcoin by using computers to solve complex mathematical puzzles. The puzzles look like this:
Take the list of the Bitcoin transactions that have occurred since the last Bitcoin was mined. Check that they’re all correctly authorized and that none of them spend money that the creator doesn’t have.
Choose a string of extra letters and numbers to add on to the end of this list (a
nonce
). This is your attempt to solve the puzzle.
Pass the list and your extra characters through an extremely complex function called the
SHA-256 hash function
(technically you pass it through the function twice). The hash function chops and slices and spins and dices the input around, seemingly (but not actually) at random. At the end it spits out a number
The puzzle that you’re trying to solve is: what combination of letters and numbers from step 2 cause the output from step 3 to be less than some small target number?
Step 1
Collect valid Bitcoin
transactions since
last block
Step 2
Add nonce
Step 3
Pass transactions and
nonce through hash
function
Step 4
Check if hash output
is less than target
NO - try again with
new nonce
Publish solution and claim reward
YES - new bitcoin
block mined!
There’s no elegant way to solve these puzzles. The only thing for Bitcoin miners to do is to guess inputs to step 2, over and over and over again, until they find one that happens to satisfy the criteria in step 4. When a miner guesses a right answer we say that they’ve “mined” a new “block”. They attach their solution to the blockchain to show that they’ve verified the transactions in the block, and they’re rewarded with new bitcoin. Their work, along with a couple of extra steps that I’ve hand-waved over, ensures that the blockchain stays safe and secure.
However, it also requires an incredible amount of electricity - around 150TWh per year, or 1% of the world’s total energy consumption. What if there was a better, more efficient way to achieve the same thing?
This is where MinorMiner and school-aged children come in. “But Bitcoin mining sounds hard!” I hear you wail. “My child has only a rudimentary grasp of basic algorithms!” True, true - but the magic is that the children on our platform don’t need to know how to mine Bitcoin, and they won’t even know that they’re doing it. Our team has converted the SHA-256 hashing algorithm used by the bitcoin blockchain into a sequence of elementary arithmetic questions that even the dullest dullard can answer. Solving a blockchain puzzle used to require understanding and executing a SHA-256 hash. Now all it takes is skipping through a few trillion simple brainteasers.
5+3=?
10*5=?
Is 102 bigger than 67? (y/n)
And so on
The kids do these sums - we take care of the rest.
How does the MinorMiner platform work?
The heart of MinorMiner is a centralised system that manages our mining. The system decomposes a SHA-256 hash computation into simple arithmetic questions, and works out which of these questions need answering next. Simple enough - but how do we get the questions to the kids? Three words: online maths quizzes.
You see, MinorMiner also has a maths learning platform that we sell to schools all over the world. Our platform isn’t p

data.title: Open Problems in Computational geometry
data.author: nill0
data.article_summary: 《开放问题项目》由Erik Demaine、Joseph Mitchell和Joseph O’Rourke编辑，旨在记录计算几何及相关领域的重要未解问题。项目始于2001年，最初发布了30个问题，现已增至75个以上。虽然不再接受新问题提交，但鼓励对现有问题进行更新，特别是已解决的问题。每个问题有唯一编号和分类，可以通过类别或问题列表浏览。涉及的类别包括排列、艺术画廊问题、着色、组合几何、数据结构、Delaunay三角剖分、切割与折叠、几何图、图绘制、图论、线性规划、下界、网格生成、最小生成树、数值计算、优化、 packing、分割等。每个问题可在Github提交更新，并提供PDF文件下载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开放性数学与计算机科学问题的收集与协作解决

不同观点：
• **支持开放问题收集与协作的系统化**：jll29认为建立一个系统化的开放问题数据库非常有用，包括为问题编号、提供状态更新和相关文献参考。他们支持继续接受新问题的提交，并希望这种活动能在数学和计算机科学的各个子领域推广。jll29还提到数学家如Terence Tao正在探索通过远程和在线方式进行合作的新方法，建议将问题清单、证明集合、现有数据集（如OEIS）以及Jupyter笔记本等工具纳入合作体系。

• **对当前数据库更新状态的关注**：wrsh07询问当前的开放问题数据库是否仍然是最新的，并提到了一些领域内有影响力的学者（如O'Rourke、Demaine、Mitchell）及其贡献，例如O'Rourke和Devadoss的书《离散与计算几何学》以及Demaine在MoMA NYC的折纸收藏。这表明wrsh07对开放问题数据库的时效性和权威性有一定关注。

• **寻求已有的解决方案**：mazsa询问是否存在类似于https://www.cs.ru.nl/~freek/100/上的解决方案，显示出对已有解决方案的兴趣，希望通过参考现有解决方案来理解或解决开放问题。

• **对文章呈现方式的个人偏好**：lordfrito表示期待看到漂亮的图片，但由于文章中没有图片，认为这篇文章不适合自己。这一评论更多是个人偏好，未涉及技术讨论。

• **新技术的潜力，特别是机器学习**：ogogmad关注新机器学习技术在解决开放问题方面的潜力，提到DeepMind发现新的极小曲面不变量的事例，并提出AI是否能发明出像同调群一样强大的概念。ogogmad认为AI可以通过构建具有预测能力的损失压缩器来实现这一点，显示出对AI技术在数学和几何问题解决中的应用前景的期待。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：虽然没有直接的争议，但不同读者对开放问题数据库的关注点有所不同。一些读者关注系统的时效性和实用性（如wrsh07和mazsa），而另一些读者则更关注技术创新和未来潜力（如jll29和ogogmad）。

• **新技术在数学问题解决中的应用前景**：ogogmad的评论引发了对机器学习和AI在数学问题解决中的潜在应用的讨论，这是一个值得注意的前沿话题。

总结：评论主要围绕开放问题数据库的构建与维护、已有解决方案的参考以及新技术在问题解决中的应用潜力展开，展现了多角度的关注和思考。

The Open Problems Project
edited by
Erik D. Demaine
,
Joseph S. B. Mitchell
,
Joseph O’Rourke
Introduction
This project originally aimed to record important open problems of interest to researchers in computational geometry and related fields. It commenced in 2001 with the publication of thirty problems in Computational Geometry Column 42
[MO01]
(see
Problems 1–30
), and then grew to over 75 problems.
While we are no longer encouraging new problem submissions, we strongly encourage updates to existing problems, especially when those problems have been solved (completely or partially). Updates should be done in the form of a Github Pull Request; see the
Github repository
.
Each problem is assigned a unique number for citation purposes. Problem numbers also indicate the order in which the problems were entered. Each problem is classified as belonging to one or more categories.
The problems are also available as a single
PDF
file.
Numerical List of All Problems
To begin navigating through the open problems, you may select from a category of interest below, or view
a list of all problems sorted numerically
.
Categorized List of All Problems
Below, each category lists the problems that are classified under that category. Note that each problem may be classified under several categories.
arrangements:
3-Colorability of Arrangements of Great Circles (Problem 44)
art galleries:
Vertex

-Floodlights (Problem 23)
coloring:

44013181.article_summary: 《开放问题项目》由Erik Demaine、Joseph Mitchell和Joseph O’Rourke编辑，旨在记录计算几何及相关领域的重要未解问题。项目始于2001年，最初发布了30个问题，现已增至75个以上。虽然不再接受新问题提交，但鼓励对现有问题进行更新，特别是已解决的问题。每个问题有唯一编号和分类，可以通过类别或问题列表浏览。涉及的类别包括排列、艺术画廊问题、着色、组合几何、数据结构、Delaunay三角剖分、切割与折叠、几何图、图绘制、图论、线性规划、下界、网格生成、最小生成树、数值计算、优化、 packing、分割等。每个问题可在Github提交更新，并提供PDF文件下载。
44013181.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开放性数学与计算机科学问题的收集与协作解决

不同观点：
• **支持开放问题收集与协作的系统化**：jll29认为建立一个系统化的开放问题数据库非常有用，包括为问题编号、提供状态更新和相关文献参考。他们支持继续接受新问题的提交，并希望这种活动能在数学和计算机科学的各个子领域推广。jll29还提到数学家如Terence Tao正在探索通过远程和在线方式进行合作的新方法，建议将问题清单、证明集合、现有数据集（如OEIS）以及Jupyter笔记本等工具纳入合作体系。

• **对当前数据库更新状态的关注**：wrsh07询问当前的开放问题数据库是否仍然是最新的，并提到了一些领域内有影响力的学者（如O'Rourke、Demaine、Mitchell）及其贡献，例如O'Rourke和Devadoss的书《离散与计算几何学》以及Demaine在MoMA NYC的折纸收藏。这表明wrsh07对开放问题数据库的时效性和权威性有一定关注。

• **寻求已有的解决方案**：mazsa询问是否存在类似于https://www.cs.ru.nl/~freek/100/上的解决方案，显示出对已有解决方案的兴趣，希望通过参考现有解决方案来理解或解决开放问题。

• **对文章呈现方式的个人偏好**：lordfrito表示期待看到漂亮的图片，但由于文章中没有图片，认为这篇文章不适合自己。这一评论更多是个人偏好，未涉及技术讨论。

• **新技术的潜力，特别是机器学习**：ogogmad关注新机器学习技术在解决开放问题方面的潜力，提到DeepMind发现新的极小曲面不变量的事例，并提出AI是否能发明出像同调群一样强大的概念。ogogmad认为AI可以通过构建具有预测能力的损失压缩器来实现这一点，显示出对AI技术在数学和几何问题解决中的应用前景的期待。

补充讨论：

data.title: Life before the web – Running a Startup in the 1980's (2016)
data.author: gscott
data.article_summary: 本文是Robert Gaskins讲述他于1984年在Forethought Inc.参与发明PowerPoint的故事的第二部分。PowerPoint是微软首次重大收购的项目。Gaskins回顾了1980年代创业的艰难，当时没有互联网，需长远规划和精准预判，且反馈和销售获取缓慢。与如今的“轻量级”网络服务和快速迭代不同，那时需要大量前期投资。PowerPoint最初针对Mac开发，但因Windows延迟发布，他们调整策略，最终PowerPoint成为Windows上首个主要演示软件，并在1990年与Windows 3.0同时发布，迅速成为国际标准。创业过程中，他们多次面临财务危机，但最终成功。Gaskins后来直接向比尔·盖茨汇报，将PowerPoint年销售额增长至1亿美元，直到1993年退休。

主要讨论点：20世纪80-90年代软件开发与交付的经历和挑战

不同观点：
• [wlindley] 分享了其公司在1980年至90年代中期开发Heathkit相关产品的经验，经历了从HDOS到MS-DOS的转型，但未在MS Windows平台上发布过产品。由于微软对开发工具的不断升级（如VB 3到VB 4，再到VB 5），他们的市场逐渐流失。这一观点强调了技术变革对小公司带来的挑战。

• [anonzzzies] 描述了在80-90年代开发和向学校交付教育软件的经历，并提到他们使用自建的BBS系统进行内部软件分发和管理工作。尽管BBS对外使用不多，但这种自给自足的开发模式让他们无需担忧第三方依赖问题。这一观点强调了自主开发和内部工具的优势。

• [saulpw] 强调了在互联网出现之前，软件公司需要通过计算机杂志编辑来接触潜在客户的困境，编辑在当时扮演了"影响者"的角色。这一观点突出了早期软件营销的局限性和依赖传统媒体的必要性。

• [jcmontx] 对比了现代软件开发与过去，表达了对现代通过代码库或分支推送来发布软件的便利性的赞赏，并认为在过去通过卡带或CD交付软件且无法更新的方式是一项巨大的挑战。这一观点突出了现代技术进步对开发者的便利。

补充讨论：
• 不同年代的开发者对技术演进的感受存在明显差异。[wlindley] 和 [anonzzzies] 都提到了技术快速变化对小公司带来的压力，而 [jcmontx] 则从现代视角出发，感慨过去交付方式的复杂性。
• 争议的焦点之一是技术升级带来的双重影响：一方面是技术进步推动了行业发展，另一方面是这种快速变化可能导致小公司失去市场竞争力。
• 另一个值得注意的点是软件分发方式的演变：从依赖实体媒介和传统媒体到现代的数字化分发和自主推送，极大改变了开发者的工作方式和市场策略。

44013046.article_content:
This is
part two
of a series of stories by
Robert Gaskins
who helped invent PowerPoint at Forethought Inc. in 1984 (
read part one here
). It was the first significant acquisition made by Microsoft.
We spoke to Robert about building a startup in the 1980s and what life was like negotiating with, and working for Microsoft. After the sale Robert reported directly to Bill Gates, heading up Microsoft’s business unit in Silicon Valley. He managed the growth of PowerPoint to
$100 million in annual sales
before his retirement in 1993.
This post looks at
what it was like running a startup in the 1980’s
and the differences Gaskins and his team experienced back then compared to running a startup today.
Here’s Gaskins in his own words …
A different age
An early mock-up of a PowerPoint slide
Developing PowerPoint in the 1980s was so incredibly different that a description of how we worked in the mid-1980s doesn’t seem to make any sense, unless one remembers that the Internet was completely unknown outside a small research community in 1984.
I had access to an ARPAnet connection when I worked at the Bell-
Northern Research laboratory in Palo Alto in the late 1970s, but I had no real experience
with it—it wasn’t something we used every day. Lots of things about the way both startups and larger software companies worked prior to the web don’t make any sense in the current age.
A software startup in the 1980s was a more difficult problem. You had to plan ahead a great distance and “call the shot” accurately, since a considerable investment was required before much in the way of feedback, let alone sales, could be available.
Today it’s the fashion to make web services in a very “lightweight” way, to offer minimally viable web products free, and to iterate rapidly as experience is gained with initial web users. Without the web, none of that was possible.
The competition
As a startup you can get crushed by a 100 pound gorilla before you even realise it sat on you. You have to be nimble enough to avoid that whatever era you are working in, whether that’s the 1980s, or 2016. Twenty years after we started developing PowerPoint Paul Graham
famously said
:
The best way to solve a problem is often to redefine it
This was a path we followed at the time. We certainly had a lot of competitors who were making presentation software for MSDOS PCs and for Apple IIs—that is, for the old command-line operating systems. I drew up a table of competitors with such products, and there were more than 30 of them, mostly selling for between $300 and $700 a copy (in 1983 !) But PowerPoint wouldn’t run on those machines.
The real competitors would be whichever successful, big software companies from that world would first make the jump to Mac and Windows. Mac had early enthusiasts, but it remained underpowered for a long time and wasn’t so attractive to businesses using MS-DOS PCs. Windows—or, at least, something like Mac’s graphical platform delivered for machines that were open and less expensive—was what customers were waiting for.
We were “writing off the entire installed base of PCs,” betting that Windows and Macintosh would grow to dominance. So these existing products were not the problem.
Windows was announced at Comdex in Fall 1983, before Mac shipped. It was much slower in shipping than anyone expected, so we redirected our first version to Mac, but when PowerPoint for Mac shipped in 1987 I thought we could  ship a Windows version in 1988. I turned out to be wrong: we didn’t ship the first PowerPoint for Windows until 1990, two years later than planned! By then we had very large competitors from the MS-DOS world, with massive numbers of users, who had only to ship a Windows version to take their users with them. Largest of all (over half the total market) was Harvard Graphics from Software Publishing Corporation (SPC).
There was also Freelance from Lotus Development, popular because it interworked with the Lotus 1–2–3 spreadsheet. WordPerfect was developing a presentation product to go with its market-leading MS-DOS word processor. People in the publishing industry liked Persuasion from Aldus which was a Mac product, but was moving to Windows as rapidly as possible.
But, as it turned out, PowerPoint was the first major presentation application for Windows, and it shipped in 1990 on the same day as the first adequate version of Windows—Bill Gates could and did use PowerPoint to announce Windows 3.0. Freelance and Persuasion shipped on Windows about one year later; Harvard Graphics shipped on Windows about two years later; and the WordPerfect product never really appeared on Windows in timely fashion. A year or two is an eternity in a rapidly exploding market; PowerPoint on Windows immediately became the international standard, and has defended that position for 25 years.
A rocky road
From mid-1984 to mid-1987, we faced the very real prospect of liquidation at least every six months. For three Christmases in a row, we took off a week for the

主要讨论点：不同方法生产石墨烯的优点及其实际应用前景

不同观点：
• [westurner的观点] 质疑使用墨水和染料生产石墨烯的优点，并提出两种替代方法：一是通过闪热技术从不分类的回收塑料中生产石墨烯，二是通过激光处理水果皮生产石墨烯，并提供了一个相关搜索链接以供参考。
   
• [th0ma5的观点] 认为通过墨水和染料生产石墨烯的突破看起来很有潜力，虽然从实验阶段转化为生产过程是另一大挑战，但这个发现本身似乎具有重大意义。

补充讨论：
• [生产方法的比较] westurner提到了几种不同的石墨烯生产方法，包括使用回收塑料和激光处理水果皮，暗示这些方法可能比使用墨水和染料更具优势。
• [实际应用的挑战] th0ma5指出，即便新方法在实验阶段显示出巨大潜力，但将其转化为实际生产过程仍面临重大挑战，这表明实际应用中的技术难题是讨论的焦点之一。
• [信息来源] westurner提供了关于“激光水果皮石墨烯”的搜索链接，表明其对该方法有一定的研究和关注，希望通过具体例子来支持其观点。

data.title: Palette lighting tricks on the Nintendo 64
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了为Nintendo 64制作的Revision 2025演示，该演示使用了烘焙光照、法线贴图和实时镜面反射技术。作者解释了他们开发的方向性环境光和法线贴图技术，这些技术简单但少见。N64由于硬件限制无法直接支持法线贴图，作者通过在CPU上进行“调色板空间”着色来实现，即仅更新调色板而无需逐像素计算光照，从而节省资源。作者还探讨了对象空间法线贴图和共享漫反射与法线贴图的调色板技术。最终，通过将环境光和直射光烘焙到顶点颜色中，实现了在N64上的光照效果，尽管光照较为粗糙，但纹理细节依然保留。

44014587.article_content:
30fps.net
- Computer Graphics & Programming with Pekka Väänänen
This article is a continuation to
my Bluesky thread
from April.
We made a Nintendo 64 demo for
Revision 2025
!
It has baked lighting with normal mapping and real-time specular shading, ahem, well sort of.
More on that later.
The beautiful song was made by
noby
with guitar performed by Moloko (
https://soundcloud.com/sou_andrade
).
Below I have some notes on the directional ambient and normal mapping techniques I developed.
They are both pretty simple in the end but I haven’t seen them used elsewhere.
But wait, normal mapping on the N64?
I knew normal mapping on the N64 was possible due to earlier experiments by fellow homebrew developers WadeTyhon and
Spooky Iluha
. I had also done
some emboss bump mapping hacks
myself.
The approach explained in this article is not new:
the renderer computes lighting directly to textures at runtime
.
It’s great because no specialized hardware support is needed and you can run arbitrary shading code on the CPU.
Too bad it’s so slow…
Shading a palette instead
So the idea is to do texture-space shading on the CPU.
But what if it’s a palette texture we’re shading?
Those are very common on the N64 anyway.
In that case it’s enough to update
only the palette
and the texture will respond as if we computed lighting for each texel.
Instant savings!
A demonstration of “palette-space” shading. When the palettes update, the full textures update too. When mapped to an object, it looks like the shading changed.
The original palette is replaced with a shaded palette and the palette texture is applied as a regular texture to an object.
With just a diffuse “dot(N,L)” lighting the results look pretty good:
Another view of the above potato-shaped rock mesh.
In the above example I also did shading in linear space by undoing the gamma correction of the color texture :) In the final demo it wasn’t possible because I split the ambient and direct light terms to be combined by N64’s RDP unit in hardware.
Object-space normal mapping
Usually normal mapping is done in tangent space.
This is way you can use repeating textures and the fine normals can modulate smoothly varying vertex normals.
A tangent-space normal map of a single color represents a smooth surface.
An object-space normal is simpler but more constrained.
Now the normal map’s texels don’t represent deviations from the vertex normals but absolute surface normals instead.
The runtime math becomes simpler – just read a color from a texture – but all surface points now need a unique texel, like in lightmaps.
An early experiment to validate the approach on a high-res normal map.
Left:
The original object-space normal map.
Right:
Compressed to a 32-color palette.
Designing a shared diffuse & normal palette
The objects have both a diffuse texture (basecolor * ao) and a normal map.
Both textures actually share the same palette indices that I generated with scikit-learn’s
K-means clustering
.
The images were interpreted as a single six-channel image for that to work.
Below is an example how the compression looks with a tangent-space normal map.
A roof tile texture compression example. An RGB diffuse texture and a normal map are both compressed to a 16-color palette image in a way that palette indices are shared. Therefore the actual image data has to be stored just once at 4 bits per pixel.
At shading time, which can happen on load or on each frame, each palette color is processed in a for loop.
A single index is used to fetch a normal and a surface diffuse color.
The CPU-side shader code then produces a new RGB color for that index.
The result of the loop is a new palette but with shading applied.
Unfortunately this approach only really works with directional lights.
It’s also difficult to represent any kind of shadows with just the palette alone.
That’s why I started looking into how baked lighting could fit in the to the equation.
Baked directional ambient and sun light
I wanted the demo to have a building with realistic lighting.
Perhaps it was a bit too ambitious😅
After a lot of deliberation, I put ambient and direct sun lighting in vertex color RGB and alpha channels, respectively.
The ambient term is further split into a directional intensity (a greyscale environment map) and color (vertex RGB with a saturation boost).
The sun is a directional light whose visibility is transmitted in vertex alpha.
The shading formula is therefore this:
ambient = vertex_rgb      * grey_irradiance_map(N)
direct  = vertex_alpha    * sun_color * dot(N, sun_dir)
color   = diffuse_texture * (ambient + direct)
Here’s how the different terms look:
Lighting decomposition.
Note how the messy “Sun visibility” vertex colors get neatly masked out by the sun (N.L) computation in the bottom right corner.
In the end the ambient and direct terms are summed to get the shaded result below.
Shaded result.

data.title: Pyrefly: A new type checker and IDE experience for Python
data.author: homarp
data.article_summary: Pyrefly是一款开源的Python类型检查工具和IDE扩展，使用Rust开发。它通过静态代码分析确保类型一致性，帮助在代码运行前发现错误，支持IDE集成和命令行使用。Pyrefly源于Instagram大规模代码库的需求，继承自Pyre类型检查器，但为了更高性能和更好的IDE体验而重新构建。其核心原则包括高性能、IDE优先、类型推断和开源合作。Pyrefly旨在实现实时代码检查、提升开发者体验，并与Python社区共同改进语言和类型系统。目前处于Alpha版本，欢迎社区反馈和贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Pyrefly（Meta推出的Python类型检查工具）的发布及其相关讨论，包括其竞争、实现语言、功能以及与现有工具的比较。

不同观点：
• **对Meta团队的担忧**（lacker）：担心Pyrefly可能像Meta之前的项目（如Atom或Flow）一样，被外部开源版本超越，从而使内部团队显得多余。建议相关负责人关注这一风险。

• **Pyrefly团队的回应**（team_pyrefly）：Pyrefly团队成员提供了官方FAQ链接，并表示愿意解答问题，试图缓解社区的疑问。

• **多个竞争者**（ThePhysicist）：目前有至少三个基于Rust的Python类型检查器（微软、Facebook、Astral），此外还有mypy。竞争激烈。

• **对Rust作为实现语言的质疑**（doug_durham）：质疑为何使用Rust实现Python工具是重要特性，认为对于非性能关键代码，使用Python编写更有利于社区支持和扩展。

• **Pyrefly的使用体验**（lucas_membrane）：用户在使用Pyrefly时遇到严格性超过Python本身的问题，但对工具发现其他问题表示肯定。同时讨论了使用SQLite管理数据流的方法是否合理。

• **编辑器集成**（xwowsersx）：对Pyrefly支持Vim/Neovim集成表示欢迎，认为这是积极的特性。

• **静态类型语言的接近程度**（liotier）：讨论Pyrefly等工具是否使Python更接近静态类型语言。

• **多语言问题的担忧**（melodyogonna）：对新Python工具多采用Rust编写表示担忧，认为这增加了多语言开发的复杂性，希望Mojo能提供解决方案。

• **Rust重写的动机**（phlakaton）：对Pyre到Pyrefly的Rust重写表示好奇，质疑是否仅因Rust流行而选择它，以及其具体优势。

• **对Facebook的不信任**（globalnode）：对Facebook产品不感兴趣，除非有重大创新如AGI。

• **对Rust重写的调侃**（weekendcode）：对Pyrefly使用Rust重写表示调侃，暗示这是预料之中的。

• **对项目范围的批评**（amelius）：认为Pyrefly试图解决太多问题，可能导致项目过于复杂。

• **与现有工具的整合建议**（kingkongjaffa）：质疑为何不直接贡献于uv、ruff和ty，而是推出新项目。

• **对Django支持的担忧**（aleksanb）：指出新类型检查器往往不支持复杂的真实世界Python代码，特别是Django，希望更多工具像TypeScript一样包容广泛的实际使用情况。

补充讨论：
• 对Pyrefly竞争态势的分析，包括与mypy及其他Rust类型检查器的比较。
• 对工具严格性和实用性的用户反馈，以及SQLite数据流管理方法的可行性讨论。
• 对多语言开发复杂性的担忧，以及对特定框架（如Django）支持的期待。

44013913.article_content:
Today we are announcing an alpha version of
Pyrefly
, an open source Python type checker and IDE extension crafted in
Rust
. Pyrefly is a static type checker that analyzes Python code to ensure type consistency and help you catch errors throughout your codebase before your code runs. It also supports IDE integration and CLI usage to give you flexibility in how you incorporate it into your workflow.
The open source community is the backbone of the Python language. We are eager to collaborate on Pyrefly with the community and improve Python’s type system and the many libraries that we all rely on.
Get started
Ready to dive in?
The official Pyrefly website
has all the details, but to quickly get started:
Install
Pyrefly on the command-line:
pip install pyrefly
.
Migrate your existing type checker configuration to Pyrefly
.
Enhance Your IDE: Download the
Pyrefly extension for VSCode
and enjoy a lightning fast IDE experience from starter projects to monorepos.
Leave feedback for us on
GitHub
.
Why we built Pyrefly
Back in 2017, we embarked on a mission to create a type checker that could handle
Instagram’s massive codebase
of typed Python. This mission led to the birth of the
Pyre
type checker, inspired by the robust designs of
Hack
and
Flow
, and written in OCaml to deliver scalable performance.
Over the years, Pyre served us well, but as the type system evolved and the need for typechecking to drive responsive IDE emerged, it was clear that we needed to take a new approach. We explored alternate solutions and leveraged community tools like
Pyright
for code navigation. But the need for an extensible type checker that can bring code navigation, checking at scale, and exporting types to other services drove us to start over, creating Pyrefly.
The principles behind Pyrefly
Today, we’re excited to unveil Pyrefly, a project
we’ve been developing openly on
GitHub
. We invite you to explore our work and try it out on your own project. While a project like Pyrefly is the sum of thousands of technical choices, a few notable principles we’ve followed are:
Performance
We want to shift checks that used to happen later on CI to happening on every single keystroke. That requires checking code at speed (on large codebases we can check 1.8 million lines of code per second!) and careful thought to incrementality and updates. Pyrefly is implemented in Rust and designed for high performance on codebases of all sizes.
IDE first
We want the IDE and command line to share a consistent view of the world, which means crafting abstractions that capture the differences without incurring unnecessary costs. Designing these abstractions from the beginning is much easier than retrofitting them, which we tried with Pyre.
Inference
Some
Python programs are typed
, but many aren’t. We want users to benefit from types even if they haven’t annotated their code – so automatically infer types for returns and local variables and display them in the IDE. What’s more, in the IDE you can even double click to insert these inferred types if you think that would make the program better.
Open source
Python is open source, and hugely popular. The
Python typing specification
is open source, which made Pyrefly vastly easier to develop. Many of the libraries Meta contributes to are open source,( e.g.,
PyTorch
).
Pyrefly is also open source,
available on GitHub
under the
MIT license
, and we encourage
pull requests
and
issue reports
. We also have a
Discord channel
for more free flowing discussions. We would love to build a community around Pyrefly.
The future of Pyrefly
We will work with the Python community to drive the language forward and improve the developer experience. Since the beginning of Pyre, we open sourced our code and contributed a number of PEPs alongside the community of type checker maintainers. We feel we can do more with Pyrefly to help Python developers leverage the benefits of types for developers, library authors, and folks just learning the language.
Meta has leveraged types in dynamic languages from the beginning and knows the significant benefits it brings to developer productivity and security. We plan to share more of our learnings and tooling with
blogs
, better types in the ecosystem and language enhancements.
Today we’re releasing Pyrefly as an alpha. At the same time, we’re busy burning down the long-tail of bugs and features aiming to remove the alpha label this Summer. Your feedback is invaluable to get there, so please give it a try and
report your bugs
or things you think can be improved. Even if Pyrefly isn’t right for your project, we would love to hear how you use types and what you would like to see improved in your editor.
Join us on the journey as we help illuminate your bugs with Pyrefly. Happy coding! 🐍✨
Hear more about Pyrefly
Check out the
episode of the Meta Tech Podcast
where several team members share their experience developing Pyrefly and technical details for how it works. We also just
talked at PyCon US
about

主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）生成的登陆页面的价值及其相比直接生成提示的优越性

不同观点：
• [nyrulez的观点] 认为直接使用LLM生成提示可能比设计一个专门的登陆页面更好。他指出，最新的模型能够很好地基于问题的种子（seed）不断优化和增强提示，直到用户满意为止。因此，他对登陆页面的必要性表示困惑。

• [nyrulez] 强调了最新LLM模型的强大能力，特别是在提示生成和优化方面的潜力。
• [1oooqooq] 提供了一个实际的应用场景，表明LLM在特定任务（如解释复杂问题）上的实用性，可能支持了登陆页面存在的合理性。

data.title: Why Are There So Many 'Alternative Devices' All of a Sudden?
data.author: fortran77
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了近期在美国一些富裕社区出现的“替代设备展会”，这些活动旨在推广功能受限的手机，以减少社交媒体对儿童心理健康的负面影响。文章作者参加了一个在康涅狄格州韦斯特波特举办的展会，看到各种设计简单、限制社交媒体使用的设备，如Barbie翻盖手机和Tin Can电话，以及升级版的Light Phone III。这些设备大多外观普通，但具有先进的家长控制功能。展会反映了家长对孩子使用智能手机的担忧，并试图提供替代方案，如简化功能的手机，以避免社交媒体的潜在危害。活动的组织者希望通过此类举措，改变当地孩子小学毕业即获得iPhone的惯例，创造更健康的数字文化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕替代设备及其功能、使用和影响的讨论

不同观点：
• **drillsteps5** 认为智能设备（如iPhone和学校发放的iPad）导致孩子过度沉迷于无意义的浏览和游戏，支持使用替代设备来帮助管理孩子的设备使用，但同时对替代设备的实际效果持怀疑态度。他提到自己不会很快给小孩智能手机，因为担心设备依赖问题。

• **spondylosaurus** 关注隐私问题，特别提到像Bark这样的第三方服务可能会审查孩子的信息，并将威胁信息报告给执法部门，这引发了对孩子隐私被侵犯的担忧。

• **ringeryless** 从社会角度出发，批评以盈利为目的的技术平台，认为这些平台的设计动机是“精神控制和市场份额”，并主张社会应该拥有一些关键的基础设施（如数据网络和大型媒体），以减少剥削和负面社会影响。

• **ValdikSS** 认为没有必要购买新的替代设备，现有的Android手机可以通过安装适当的软件实现同样的功能。他主张开发功能简单、电池寿命长的手机，并提出“平静技术设备”的概念，如小米手环，可以减少对智能手机的频繁检查。

• **pedalpete** 认为文章讨论的重点不应仅限于替代设备，而应更广泛地关注设备如何保障孩子的安全。他提到设备本身不重要，软件功能才是关键，并分享了自己在神经技术和睡眠技术领域的工作经验，认为这些新技术才是真正的“替代设备”。

• **amelius** 提出立法建议，要求所有设备都应该是通用计算设备，用户拥有完全控制权，这样任何设备都可以根据个人需求变成“替代设备”。

• **Aerbil313** 分享了自己作为AuDHD患者的经历，表示无法使用不受限制的智能手机，因为这会严重影响生活和健康。他支持开发不能滥用的智能设备，并希望建立一家生产这种设备的公司，以帮助像他一样有特殊需求的人。

补充讨论：
- **隐私与安全**：spondylosaurus对第三方服务审查孩子信息的做法表示担忧，认为这可能导致隐私泄露和不必要的执法介入。
- **设备依赖与成瘾**：drillsteps5和Aerbil313都提到了设备依赖问题，尤其是对孩子和有特殊需求的人的影响。
- **技术与社会责任**：ringeryless强调技术平台的盈利动机带来的负面社会影响，主张社会应对关键基础设施拥有控制权。
- **替代设备的必要性与实现方式**：ValdikSS和pedalpete对替代设备的必要性持不同看法，前者认为现有设备可以通过软件实现类似功能，后者则认为新技术和设备可以带来行为改变和新的可能性。

争议焦点：
- **隐私与安全**：如何在保障孩子安全的同时，保护他们的隐私不受第三方服务侵犯。
- **设备依赖**：如何在提供便利和功能的同时，避免设备成瘾和依赖问题。
- **替代设备的必要性**：是否需要开发新的替代设备，还是通过软件改造现有设备来实现类似功能。

On a recent commute to work, I texted my distant family about our fantasy baseball league, which was nice because I felt connected to them for a second. Then I switched apps and became enraged by a stupid opinion I saw on X, which I shouldn’t be using anymore due to its
advanced toxicity
and mind-numbing inanity. Many minutes passed before I was able to stop reading the stupid replies to the stupid original post and relax the muscles of my face.
This is the duality of the phone: It connects me to my loved ones, and sometimes I think it’s ruining my life. I need it and I want it, but sometimes I hate it and I fear it. Many people have to navigate this problem—and it may be at its worst for parents, who’ve recently been drowned in media suggesting that smartphones and social media
might be harming their children’s mental health
, but who also want their kids to enjoy technology’s benefits and prepare themselves for adult life in a digital age.
Read: No one knows exactly what social media is doing to teens
It was with this tension in mind that I rode a train last week to the town of Westport, Connecticut. There, a parent-led group called OK to Delay had organized an “Alternative Device Fair” for families who wanted to learn about different kinds of phones that were intentionally limited in their functionality. (There would be no frowning at X with these devices, because most of them block social media.) Similar bazaars have been
popping up
here and there over the past year, often in the more affluent suburbs of the tristate area. Westport’s fair, modeled after
an event
held last fall in Rye, New York, was set up in a spacious meeting room in the most immaculate and well-appointed public library I’ve ever seen. When I arrived, about 30 minutes after the start of the four-hour event, it was bustling. The chatter was already at a healthy, partylike level.
The tables set up around the room each showed off a different device. One booth had a Barbie-branded flip phone; another was offering a retro-styled “landline” phone called the Tin Can. But most of the gadgets looked the same—generic, rectangular smartphones. Each one, however, has its own special, restricted app store, and a slew of parental-control features that are significantly more advanced than what would have been available only a few years ago. One parent showed me her notepad, on which she was taking detailed notes about the minute differences among these phones; she planned to share the information with an online group of parents who hadn’t been able to come. Another mom told me that she’d be asking each booth attendant how easy it would be for kids to hack the phone system and get around the parent controls—something you can see kids discussing
openly on the internet
all the time.
A couple of years ago, I explored
the “dumb phone” trend
, a cultural curiosity about returning to the time before smartphones by eschewing complex devices and purchasing something simpler and deliberately limited. One of the better phones I tried then was the Light Phone II, which I disliked only because it was so tiny that I constantly feared that I would break or lose it. At the library, I chatted with Light Phone’s Dan Fox, who was there to show people the latest version of the device. The Light Phone III is larger and thicker and has a camera, but it still uses a black-and-white screen and prohibits web browsing and social-media apps. He told me that it was his third alternative-device event in a week. He’d also been to Ardsley, a village in New York’s Westchester County, and to the Upper East Side, in Manhattan. He speculated that kids like the Light Phone because it doesn’t require all the rigmarole about filters and settings and
parents
. It was designed for adults, and therefore seems cool, and was designed in Brooklyn, which makes it seem cooler. (Fox then left early to go to a Kendrick Lamar concert with his colleagues.)
Read: Phones will never be fun again
The crowded room in Westport was reflective of
the broad concern
about the effect that social media may have on children and teenagers. But it was also a very specific expression of it. Explaining the impetus for hosting the marketplace, Becca Zipkin, a co-founder of the Westport branch of OK to Delay, told me that it has become the standard for kids in the area to receive an iPhone as an elementary-school graduation present. One of her group’s goals is to push back on this ritual and create a different culture in their community. “This is not a world in which there are no options,” she said.

data.author: flashblaze
data.article_summary: Harmonic for Hacker News 是一款现代、快速、设计周到的Android Hacker News客户端，可在Google Play下载。该项目自2020年起由Simon Halvdansson个人开发，由于2021年开始攻读博士学位，投入时间减少。Harmonic未使用Kotlin或最新的Android API，但功能齐全、运行良好。项目开源旨在让用户提交修复问题或添加功能的Pull Requests，但不考虑完全重写为Kotlin。应用功能包括基本账户操作、Material 3设计、多种主题和高度定制化选项，性能良好。目前有698颗星和49个分支，支持社区贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对应用的评价及功能建议

不同观点：
• FloatArtifact对应用的导入导出功能表示赞赏，并建议此功能不仅限于书签，还可以扩展到设置。此外，他们对能够在archive.org上查看文章的选项表示喜欢，因为这解决了付费墙问题。
• elcapitan对应用的优势表示疑问，指出由于有许多类似的客户端，希望了解这个应用的独特之处，但未得到具体解答。
• sotsoguk认为应用名称应包含"Harmonic"，以反映其作为现代Android HN客户端的特性，暗示当前名称可能不够明确。
• ItsHarper和hahn-kev都是该应用的长期用户，对应用表示高度赞赏，hahn-kev特别提到从Harmonic客户端发表评论，进一步支持sotsoguk的命名建议。
• mikae1提出将应用发布到F-Droid的建议，以扩大其分发渠道，但未详细说明理由。
• atmanactive回应mikae1的建议，表示在F-Droid上未能找到该应用，暗示可能存在分发渠道不足的问题。
• methuselah_in简单表达了对应用外观和功能的肯定。

补充讨论：
- 关于应用命名的讨论，sotsoguk建议加入"Harmonic"以突出其特性，而其他用户如hahn-kev的使用体验也从侧面支持了这个命名建议。
- 用户FloatArtifact特别关注内容访问的便捷性，尤其是对付费墙内容的替代访问方式表示赞赏。
- 关于应用在F-Droid上可用性的讨论，mikae1提出建议但未详细说明理由，而atmanactive则验证了当前不可用的状态。
- elcapitan对应用独特性的疑问未得到解答，可能暗示需要更多关于应用特点和优势的介绍。

Harmonic for Hacker News
Harmonic for Hacker News is an Android Hacker News client which is meant to be modern, fast and well thought out. You can find it on Google Play for download.
This has been my personal side project since 2020 and since starting my PhD in 2021 the time I have to dedicate to Harmonic has decreased. My personal philosophy on side projects is that the most important thing is building something that is actually shipped. Since much of my knowledge on building Android apps is ~10 years old, Harmonic does not use Kotlin or the latest Android API's and is probably not the easiest app to dig into the source code of. However, it is shipped, and it works fairly well in my opinion at least. :)
The purpose of open-sourcing Harmonic is thus mainly to enable interested users to submit pull requests fixing issues or adding features. I would like to still be able to find my way around the app's code so I am not looking for a full Kotlin rewrite but if you have something you'd like to see fixed or added I am  very open to PR's. I'll still commit things myself when I have time.
Features
Basic account functionality: log in, vote, comment, and submit
Material 3 design with some nice animations
Several themes including full black
A ton of customization options, bordering on feature creep
Fast!

data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了三位科学家声称普通重物质也能像黑洞一样发出霍金辐射，甚至导致死星逐渐消失。他们认为这会导致宇宙比预期更快终结。然而，这一观点遭到其他研究者的反驳，指出他们的计算使用了不准确的近似方法，实际上静态质量的引力场不会产生粒子-反粒子对。专家早已在1975年的研究中明确了这一点，即在静态时空中，真空是稳定的，不会自发产生粒子。尽管该论文发表在权威期刊上，但并未得到物理学界的广泛认可。文章批评了一些科学记者轻信新闻稿，传播了错误信息。作者建议应咨询领域专家以辨别此类研究的可信度。

44015872.article_content:
Azimuth
Home
About
Dead Stars Don’t Radiate
Three guys claim that any heavy chunk of matter emits Hawking radiation, even if it’s not a black hole:
• Michael F. Wondrak, Walter D. van Suijlekom and Heino Falcke,
Gravitational pair production and black hole evaporation
,
Phys. Rev. Lett.
130
(2023), 221502.
Now they’re getting more publicity by claiming this means that the universe will fizzle out sooner than we expected.
They’re claiming
, for example, that a dead, cold star will emit Hawking radiation, and thus slowly lose mass and eventually disappear!
They admit that this would violate baryon conservation: after all, the protons and neutrons in the star would have to go away somehow!  They admit they don’t know how this would work.  They just say that the gravitational field of the star will create particle-antiparticle pairs that will slowly radiate away, forcing the dead star to lose mass
somehow
to conserve energy.
If experts thought this had even a chance of being true, it would be the biggest thing since sliced bread—at least in the field of quantum gravity.  Everyone would be writing papers about it, because if true it would be revolutionary.   It would overturn calculations by experts which say that a stationary chunk of matter doesn’t emit Hawking radiation.  It would also mean that quantum field theory in curved spacetime can only be consistent if baryon number fails to be conserved!  This would be utterly shocking.
But in fact, these new papers have had almost zero effect on physics.  There’s a short rebuttal, here:
• Antonio Ferreiro José Navarro-Salas and Silvia Pla,
Comment on “Gravitational pair production and black hole evaporation”
,
Phys. Rev. Lett.
133
(2024), 229001.
It explains that these guys used a crude approximation that gives wrong results even in a simpler problem.   Similar points are made here:
• E. T. Akhmedov, D. V. Diakonov and C. Schubert,
Complex effective actions and gravitational pair creation
,
Phys. Rev. D.
110
, 105011.
Unfortunately, it seems the real experts on quantum field theory in curved spacetime have not come out and mentioned the
correct
way to think about this issue, which has been known at least since 1975.  To them—or maybe I should dare to say “us”—it’s just
well known
that the gravitational field of a static mass does not cause the creation of particle-antiparticle pairs.
Of course, the referees should have rejected Wondrak, van Suijlekom and Falcke’s papers.  But apparently none of those referees were experts on the subject at hand.  So you can’t trust a paper just because it appears in a supposedly reputable physics journal.  You have to actually understand the subject and assess the paper yourself, or talk to some experts you trust.
If I were a science journalist writing an article about a supposedly shocking development like this, I would email some experts and check to see if it’s for real.  But plenty of science journalists don’t bother with that anymore: they just believe the press releases.  So now we’re being bombarded with lazy articles like these:
•
Universe will die “much sooner than expected,” new research says
,
CBS News
, May 13, 2025.
• Sharmila Kuthunur,
Scientists calculate when the universe will end—it’s sooner than expected
,
Space.com
, 15 May 2025.
• Jamie Carter,
The universe will end sooner than thought, scientists say
,
Forbes
, 16 May 2025.
The list goes on; these are just three.   There’s no way what I say can have much effect against such a flood of misinformation.  As Mark Twain said, “A lie can travel around the world and back again while the truth is lacing up its boots.”  Actually he probably didn’t say that—but everyone keeps saying he did, illustrating the point perfectly.
Still, there might be a few people who both care and don’t already know this stuff.  Instead of trying to give a mini-course here, let me simply point to an explanation of how things really work:
• Abhay Ashtekar and Anne Magnon,
Quantum fields in curved space-times
,
Proceedings of the Royal Society
,
346
(1975), 375–394.
It’s technical, so it’s not easy reading if you haven’t studied quantum field theory and general relativity, but that’s unavoidable.  It shows that in a static spacetime there is a well-defined concept of ‘vacuum’, and the vacuum is stable.  Jorge Pullin pointed out the key sentence for present purposes:
Thus, if the underlying space-time admits a everywhere time-like Killing field, the vacuum state is indeed stable and phenomena such as the spontaneous creation of particles do not occur.
This condition of having an “everywhere time-like Killing field” says that a spacetime has time translation symmetry.  Ashtekar and Magnon also assume that spacetime is globally hyperbolic and that the wave equation for a massive spin-zero particle has a smooth solution given smooth initial data.  All this lets us define a concept of energy for solutions of this equation.  It also lets us split solutions into positive-frequency solutions, which cor

data.title: Show HN: I built a knife steel comparison tool
data.author: p-s-v
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了刀具钢材的性能对比，包括耐腐蚀性、韧性、刃口保持力和易 sharpening 程度四个方面，评分范围为1-10。用户可以选择最多5种钢材进行比较。文章列出了多组钢材的对比分析图表，如1095 vs 5160、154CM vs S30V、20CV vs M390等，涵盖多种常见和高端刀具钢材，帮助用户了解不同钢材在各项性能上的表现，以便做出更好的选择。文章提供了超过150个详细对比，其中147个包含图表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：刀具钢材性能比较工具的数据来源、可信度及其相关讨论

不同观点：
• [kurthr] 认为数据应包括硬度（如HRC值）以支持雷达图展示的性能，并指出热处理和开刃角度对刀具性能的影响被忽略。他强调热处理对刀具性能至关重要，且不同钢材能支持的开刃角度不同。
• [LooseMarmoset] 作为刀具制造者，提出应加入80CRV、1084、1075等常用钢材，并指出440钢有不同等级。他还建议展示锰含量和钢材硬化深度，以帮助判断是否能形成“刃纹”（hamon）。
• [ZYbCRq22HbJ2y7] 质疑数据来源及其可信度，认为部分数据可能由大语言模型生成，且部分图表和数据存在缺失或混乱。
• [eichin] 提到该工具与另一个刀具数据库有交叉，但指出该项目仅有市场名称而缺乏具体钢材数据，不过也提供了原始数据链接供用户自行分析。

补充讨论：
• [hunter-gatherer] 表示工具很有用，但已经购买了CPM Magnacut钢材的刀具，尚未进行磨刀测试。
• [abcd_f] 询问是否计划加入日本钢材，并提供了一个参考链接。
• [reconnecting] 对如何“解码”钢材类型表示好奇，并以二战时期的Kabelmesser口袋刀为例，指出高碳钢的稀缺性。
• [keisborg] 探讨了刀具钢材性能的平衡问题，质疑是否能同时拥有良好的边缘保持性、易磨性和韧性，并希望看到性能权衡的实例。
• [bberenberg] 建议按多边形总面积对钢材进行排名。
• [out-of-ideas] 提出在比较时保持颜色静态以提高图表可读性。
• [williadc] 建议加入Sandvik 14c28n钢材，常见于预算刀具。
• [adamgordonbell] 提到陶瓷刀的优缺点，指出其超锋利但易碎。
• [nntwozz] 建议加入硼钢。

争议焦点：
• 数据来源及其可信度是主要争议点，[ZYbCRq22HbJ2y7] 对数据的真实性提出质疑，而[kurthr] 和 [LooseMarmoset] 则关注数据的完整性和实用性。
• 热处理和开刃角度对刀具性能的影响也被深入讨论，[kurthr] 强调其重要性，而[LooseMarmoset] 则从刀具制造者角度提出具体建议。

data.title: How to have the browser pick a contrasting color in CSS
data.author: Kerrick
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了一种新的CSS功能——`contrast-color()`，它可以让浏览器根据指定颜色自动选择黑色或白色文本，以确保更好的对比度。在设计多色按钮时，这个功能特别有用，开发者只需定义背景色，浏览器会自动选择适当的对比色作为文本颜色。例如，可以将按钮的背景色设置为变量`--button-color`，文本颜色使用`contrast-color(var(--button-color))`。

不过，文章也提醒读者，虽然`contrast-color()`能帮助选择对比色，但不保证完全符合无障碍标准（如WCAG 2）。某些中色调背景可能仍会导致对比不足的问题。因此，开发和设计团队仍需手动检查颜色的对比度，确保可访问性。当前，Safari技术预览版中实现了这一功能，但实际效果依赖于WCAG 2的对比度算法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：为确保网页可访问性，自动选择对比色（如黑/白）的工具和方法

不同观点：
• seanwilson：开发了一个工具（Inclusive Colors），基于WCAG/ACPA标准生成具有可预测对比度的色板，并指出ACPA标准在深色主题上比WCAG更严格。还提到未来可能会有更复杂的工具来支持更丰富的颜色选择。
• qfr：提出使用LCH颜色空间的CSS方法，通过计算自动选择对比色。
• jjcm：认为对于简单项目，自动选择对比色是有效的，但对于需要WCAG合规的生产级别项目，建议使用语义化设计令牌来确保对比度和视觉一致性，并能轻松实现深色/浅色主题。
• econ：分享了过去使用系统颜色遇到的对比度问题，并通过JavaScript计算颜色对比度解决，同时提到使用RGB平均值的简单对比方法。
• mediumsmart：指出在大型项目中管理颜色细节的困难，建议在设计阶段仔细检查按钮颜色对比度。
• politelemon：质疑浏览器自动选择对比色的可靠性和可预测性，认为这应是UX团队在设计阶段的工具，而非浏览器默认行为。
• lancekey：提到过去使用YIQ值的方法来选择对比色。
• akkartik：开发了一个工具，在创作阶段强制要求颜色对比度，若不符合要求则报错。
• jbritton：希望有针对伪类（如active, focus, hover等）的颜色建议。
• Hyperlisk：分享了一个动态文本对比度的CSS方法。
• ZYbCRq22HbJ2y7：提到CSS工作组草案中关于颜色对比度的未来特性。
• rendaw：认为选择对比色不应比选择背景色更困难，质疑该功能的实用性，并指出其在处理复杂背景下的不足。
• andix：询问是否有在构建时运行的替代方案，如基于SASS或Tailwind的工具。
• crtasm：提到某些浏览器不支持contrast-color()功能，建议使用支持的浏览器如Safari技术预览版。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于浏览器自动选择对比色的可靠性和适用范围，部分开发者认为这是UX团队在设计阶段应处理的问题。
• 不同方法的优劣被广泛讨论，包括使用WCAG/ACPA标准、LCH颜色空间、RGB平均值等方法。
• 大型项目中的颜色管理和语义化设计令牌的应用被认为是更有效的解决方案，特别是在确保WCAG合规和视觉一致性方面。

44015367.article_content:
How to have the browser pick a contrasting color in CSS
May 13, 2025
by
Jen Simmons
Have you ever wished you could write simple CSS to declare a color, and then have the browser figure out whether black or white should be paired with that color? Well, now you can, with
contrast-color()
. Here’s how it works.
Imagine we’re building a website or a web app, and the design calls for a bunch of buttons with different background colors. We can create a variable named
--button-color
to handle the background color. And then assign that variable different values from our design system in different situations.
Sometimes the button background will be a dark color, and the button text should be white to provide contrast. Other times, the background will be a lighter color, and the text should be black. Like this:
Now, of course, we could use a second variable for the text color and carefully define the values for
--button-color
and
--button-text-color
at the same time, in pairs, to ensure the choice for the text color is the right one. But, on a large project, with a large team, carefully managing such details can become a really hard task to get right. Suddenly a dark button has unreadable black text, and users can’t figure out what to do.
It’d be easier if we could just tell our CSS to make the text black/white, and have the browser pick which to use — whichever one provides more contrast with a specific color. Then we could just manage our many background colors, and not worry about the text color.
That’s exactly what the
contrast-color()
function will let us do.
contrast-color()
We can write this in our CSS:
color
:
contrast-color
(
purple
);
And the browser will set
color
to either black or white, whichever choice provides better contrast with
purple
.
Let’s style our button. We’ll set the button background color to our variable. And we’ll define the text color to be the contrasting black/white choice that pairs with that variable.
button
{
background-color
:
var
(
--button-color
);
color
:
contrast-color
(
var
(
--button-color
));
}
Now we only need to define one color, and the other follows! When we change the button color, the browser will reconsider whether the text should be black or white, and choose fresh the option with more contrast.
For fun, let’s also define a hover color using
Relative Color Syntax
, and now one variable determines four colors — the default button color & the text to go with it, plus the hover color & the text to go with that.
:root
{
--button-color
:
purple
;
--hover-color
:
oklch
(
from
var
(
--button-color
)
calc
(
l
+
.2
)
c
h
);
}
button
{
background-color
:
var
(
--button-color
);
color
:
contrast-color
(
var
(
--button-color
));
text-box
:
cap
alphabetic
;
/* vertically centers the text */
}
button
:hover
{
background-color
:
var
(
--hover-color
);
color
:
contrast-color
(
var
(
--hover-color
));
}
Here’s a demo of the result
. Try it in
Safari Technology Preview
, where you can change the button color dynamically.
Accessibility considerations and contrast algorithms
Now, it might be tempting to believe that
contrast-color()
will magically solve all contrast accessibility concerns all by itself, and your team will never have to think about color contrast again. Nope, that’s not the case. At all.
Using the
contrast-color()
function does not guarantee that the resulting pair of colors will be accessible. It’s quite possible to pick a color (in this case a background color) that will not have enough contrast with either black or white. It’s still up to the humans involved — designers, developers, testers, and more — to ensure there’s enough contrast.
In fact, if you try out
our demo
in Safari Technology Preview now (as this article is published in May 2025), you’ll find many of the pairings with mid-tone background colors don’t result in enough contrast. It often seems like the wrong choice is being made. For example, this #317CFF blue returns a contrast-color of black.
When white is clearly the better choice for perceptual contrast.
What is happening here? Why is the less-contrasting choice being made?
Well, the current implementation in Safari Technology Preview is using the contrast algorithm officially defined in
WCAG 2
(Web Content Accessibility Guidelines version 2). If we put this color blue through a well-respected
color contrast checker at WebAIM
, it does clearly recommend using black for the text color, not white. WCAG 2 is the current authoritative standard for accessibility on the web, required by law in many places.
The WCAG 2 algorithm calculates black-on-#317CFF as having a contrast ratio of 5.45:1, while white-on-#317CFF has 3.84:1. The
contrast-color()
function is simply choosing the option with the bigger number — and 5.45 is bigger than 3.84.
Testing black versus white on a medium-dark blue in the
WCAG 2 color contrast checker at Web AIM
.

data.title: How I fixed the infamous Basilisk II Windows “Black Screen” bug in 2013
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者Doug Brown在2013年如何修复了Basilisk II在Windows系统上的“黑屏” bug。Basilisk II是一款68k Mac模拟器，在较新的Windows版本（如Vista和7）上运行时，常出现启动后黑屏无法启动Mac系统的问题，而Windows 2000和XP则较少出现此问题。作者通过添加调试输出追踪代码运行情况，最终发现问题出在视频刷新函数`video_refresh_window_vosf()`中。当视频功能未能正确标记需要更新时，就会出现黑屏。虽然旧版本的Basilisk II（build 142）没有此问题，但缺乏性能改进。作者通过调试解决了这个长期存在的bug，使得模拟器在Windows 7上能够正常运行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对技术调试、系统兼容性和模拟器使用的讨论。

不同观点：
• [RJIb8RBYxzAMX9u] 认为现代计算资源的丰富令人惊叹，通过在现代系统上模拟旧系统来进行调试是令人惊讶的进展。他通过个人经历，回忆自己最早使用68k Mac的经历，并感叹当时无法想象会有如今的计算能力。

• [MBCook] 从技术角度出发，提出内存分配问题可能与Vista中引入的ASLR（地址空间布局随机化）有关，这是微软在提升系统安全性时所做的改变。他还对最初的内存分配方式表示好奇，希望了解其原因。

• [rcarmo] 分享了自己在GNOME环境下运行BasiliskII模拟器时遇到的分辨率问题，尽管进行了手动设置调整，但模拟器仍未能按预期运行，反映出在现代环境中运行旧软件的实际困难。

• [cardanome] 回忆了自己在PlayStation Portable上运行Basilisk 2的经历，虽然不确定这样做的实际意义，但对此感到高兴，似乎更关注于模拟旧系统的趣味性，而非其实际用途或技术细节。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点并不明显，但可以看出用户对现代系统上运行旧系统或软件的实际可行性和目的存在不同看法。[RJIb8RBYxzAMX9u] 和 [cardanome] 更关注于技术的进步和趣味性，而 [rcarmo] 和 [MBCook] 则更关注技术细节和实际问题。

• 不同用户对模拟器使用的体验和关注点各不相同，从技术调试、分辨率问题到个人娱乐使用，展现了技术爱好者在使用旧系统模拟器时的多样化需求和挑战。
